name: The Shilla Seoul
insider_take: This legendary palace of Korean hospitality has been Seoul's crown jewel since 1979, where traditional elegance meets modern luxury in the heart of Jung-gu district.
whats_special: The Shilla Seoul sits majestically on 23 acres of meticulously landscaped gardens, featuring Korea's largest hotel art collection with over 2,000 pieces including national treasures. The property's unique stepped architecture mimics traditional Korean palace design, while its location offers stunning views of Namsan Park and N Seoul Tower.
pro_tip: Book a room on the executive floors for exclusive access to the Executive Lounge, which offers some of the best panoramic city views and complimentary Korean royal court cuisine tastings.
dont_miss: The hotel's legendary Guerlain Spa, Korea's first luxury European spa, and the award-winning La Yeon restaurant - the first hotel restaurant in Korea to earn three Michelin stars. Take an evening stroll through the hotel's traditional Korean garden, illuminated beautifully at night.
pros: Iconic Seoul landmark nestled within a serene forested mountain setting yet minutes from the city center
World-class dining spanning acclaimed Korean, Japanese, and Western restaurants under one roof
Expansive luxury spa and indoor pool offering a comprehensive wellness retreat experience
Impeccable white-glove service consistently praised for attentiveness and cultural warmth
Premier duty-free shopping arcade and proximity to Itaewon and Myeongdong districts
cons: Hillside location requires shuttle or taxi access, making walkability to some attractions limited
Premium price point positions it among Seoul's most expensive luxury accommodations
